patch.objective: Develop a collaborative safety plan with a client at risk
secondaryObjectives: Assess risk of suicide, homicide, self-injury and relationship violence at intake and throughout counseling

sources.note: Relayed from the REQ-239 NCE sessions (read 2026-11-11), not re-read for this band: the objective title is the course's own, built from this outline. Current outline; NBCC's new blueprint takes effect 2027-07-01.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

sources.cite: Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS), Screen Version: wish to be dead; suicidal thoughts; thoughts with method; intent without plan; intent with plan; suicidal behavior (ever, and how long ago)
sources.note: Relayed from the NCMHCE case ncmhce-suicide-safety-plan, not re-read for this band; its note: Re-read 2026-11-11. The screen's questions are paraphrased; it does not itself set risk levels or actions, which come from the counselor's formulation and local protocol.

sources.cite: Stanley B, Brown GK. Safety planning intervention: a brief intervention to mitigate suicide risk. Cogn Behav Pract 2012;19:256-264; SPRC summary of the six steps
sources.note: Relayed from the NCMHCE case ncmhce-suicide-safety-plan, not re-read for this band; its note: Read for the EPPP sessions on 2026-11-10, not re-read here. Steps: warning signs; internal coping strategies; people and social settings that provide distraction; people to ask for help; professionals or agencies to contact in a crisis; making the environment safe (restricting lethal means). Presented as an alternative to no-suicide contracts, which 'never [have] been rigorously evaluated and shown effective'.

sources.cite: ACA Code of Ethics (2014): A.1.c counseling plans made jointly; A.1.d support network involvement; B.2.a serious and foreseeable harm
sources.note: Relayed from the NCMHCE case ncmhce-suicide-safety-plan, not re-read for this band; its note: The current code per counseling.org (read 2026-11-11). A.1.d's text was not quoted here; the scenario involves her roommate only with her consent.

brief.situation: Marisol Vega, 26 (a fictional client), a certified nursing assistant, came to your outpatient practice two weeks ago with low mood after a breakup and an eviction notice; she shares an apartment with her friend Jess and is close to her brother Mateo, 12. At intake she denied suicidal thoughts. Last night at 23:40 she left a voicemail: 'I don't see the point anymore. Sorry. See you Thursday.' This is Thursday's session, her second. You are a licensed clinical mental health counselor; you have 50 minutes.
